newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends steady, trading seen dull.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends steady, trading seen dull.

text.p: Rubber futures closed mostly steady on Friday as mild shortcovering allowed the market to shrug off lower prices in Japan, dealers said.
"There was some shortcovering for RSS3 rubber, but the overall volume in the market was so flat. There's still no major buying from overseas consumers," a local rubber trader said.

"It's still a bearish market. Trading was basically flat and lifeless. I'm not sure the mood will change all that much next week. Buying sentiment remains soft and most consumers are just living on a hand-to-mouth basis," another dealer said.
The local market bucked lower prices in Tokyo, where the benchmark April contract settled 0.8 yen down at 142.5.
Kobe's April contract settled at 142.3 from the previous 142.9 yen.
At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 was seen at 127.50 U.S. cents a kg from yesterday's settlement of 128.25 cents.
January RSS1 was seen at 183.00-185.00 Singapore cents (US$1.31-$1.32) a kg from the previous 183.50 cents.
January TSR20 was seen at 176.00-178.00 Singapore cents (US$1.25-$1.27) a kg from 177.25 cents. (US$1-S$1.40) -- Rene Pastor (65-870-3305)
